name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans 18 points Democratic and the seat is held by a Democratic incumbent
Walkinshaw holds a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising edge plus $2.7M in outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
No public polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Walkinshaw's overwhelming financial advantage over Purves, and market pricing near 97 percent all point to a comfortable hold. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting a contest, the fundamentals dominate the forecast.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or surprise polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal of movement, though nothing currently points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
James Walkinshaw, the Democratic incumbent, seeks his first full term representing a Northern Virginia district that leans 18 points Democratic. He faces Republican Arthur Purves, a first-time candidate, and Green nominee Dianne Blais in the general election.

The financial picture is lopsided: Walkinshaw has raised about $2.8 million and benefits from roughly $2.7 million in outside support, while Purves has raised about $31,000. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97 percent. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
